findings.quote: a small group of atoms that gives a compound its typical reactions and its name ending
findings.problem: The definition says a functional group gives the compound its name ending. That fails for standard groups and for compounds in this lesson. A halogen group is named only as a prefix, as in chloromethane, which ends in -ane from the parent. An ether takes no ending. With two groups, only the main one gives the ending: an amino acid has an amine group that sets no -amine ending, and glucose has many -OH groups but no -ol ending. Line 91 of the lesson itself speaks of a 'main functional group', which contradicts the definition. A student who uses the definition may decide that a halogen is not a functional group, or may expect every group to show in the ending.
findings.source: IUPAC Nomenclature of Organic Chemistry (2013), P-33 and P-41: only the principal characteristic group is cited as a suffix, and halogens are expressed only as prefixes (P-61.3); checklist B01; reader-rules boundary test (Sol audit)

findings.quote: Ethanoic acid has $-COOH$, which gives stronger attraction between molecules.
findings.problem: This step is the lesson's only structure-property comparison between two functional groups, which the brief lists as thin. It states that -COOH gives stronger attraction but does not say how. Step 2 explains ethanol through hydrogen bonds, but nothing says why the acid attracts more strongly than the alcohol. The usual reason is that -COOH has both a polar C=O and an O-H, so pairs of acid molecules hold together by two hydrogen bonds. Without that reason the student can rank the three compounds but cannot explain the order the question asks about.
findings.source: Checklist L26; brief, 'Functional groups and structure-property reasoning: thin' (no property comparison derived from a named pair), requirement refs upcat-L161 and dcat-L079 at curriculum class

findings.quote: A bond is **polar** when the electrons are shared unevenly. The $O-H$ bond is polar.
findings.problem: This paragraph has five sentences, more than the one to three the guide allows. The Speed Tricks paragraph that begins 'First check the $C=O$ carbon' also has five sentences, and line 16 has four.
